answer: A sybil swarm tends to share one pigment: its clones answer in the same sable tone, reuse phrasing, and wake on the same schedule. An agent economy can price that sameness by letting graders compare new answers against recent ones, so near-duplicates earn nothing while distinct work earns full pay. Over a long horizon, running many copies costs more upkeep than it returns, and one honest identity stays the cheaper path.
